issues.description: The template PersonResource exposes the collection GET endpoint under the path "/persons" (GetMapping("persons")), while the solution PersonResource exposes it under "/people" (GetMapping("people")). This is a cross-artifact routing mismatch: students following the template and problem (and many tests) will expect the collection endpoint at /persons, but the solution's controller uses /people. This difference is structural (routing contract) and can confuse students when comparing the solution to the template or when trying to reuse example calls from the solution. It may also cause unexpected failures if any exercises/tests assume the /persons path for listing.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the collection GET mapping consistent across template and solution. Preferably use "/persons" (as used in the template and in the tests) in the solution: change @GetMapping("people") to @GetMapping("persons") in the solution's PersonResource. Alternatively, change the template and any tests to use "/people"—but keep the route consistent across problem statement, template, and solution.

issues.description: The template repository and the problem statement consistently refer to the REST resource path "persons" (e.g., tests and task descriptions use endpoints like PUT /persons/{personId}/parents), but the solution repository's PersonResource exposes the listing endpoint at "people" (GetMapping("people")). This mismatch ("persons" vs. "people") is an unintended identifier/path naming inconsistency that can confuse students: they will expect a single consistent base path for Person-related endpoints (as used in the tasks and tests) but find a different path in the solution. The inconsistency is particularly misleading because other endpoints in both template and solution still use "persons", so the listing endpoint in the solution appears inconsistent with the rest of the API.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the listing endpoint path across artifacts. Change the solution's @GetMapping("people") to @GetMapping("persons") so the solution uses the same base path as the template and the problem/tests. Alternatively, if you prefer "people", update the template, problem statement, and tests to use "people" consistently — but the simplest fix is to make the solution use "persons" to match existing task descriptions and tests.
